name: BOLT post-link optimization (via cargo-pgo)
baseline: A PGO-optimized release binary without BOLT
verdict_reason: BOLT adds a further gain on top of PGO, but the measured gains are small and vary: about 6.1% for Android's rustc and a 1.8% mean cycle reduction for librustc_driver.so in rust-lang CI. It enlarges binaries, needs relocations kept in the binary, and cargo-pgo marks its BOLT support experimental.
tier_reason: Measured by Google's Android toolchain team and the rust-lang project on rustc, independent of cargo-pgo.
claimed_speedup: Android rustc: ~6.1% faster than the PGO-only compiler (~24.7% over baseline) at ~10.9% larger size; rust-lang librustc_driver.so: -1.8% mean cycles across primary benchmarks, with a 34 MiB (+48%) larger library
workload: rustc compiling Android's Rust components; rustc-perf primary benchmarks
toolchain: llvm-bolt applied to libLLVM, libstd and librustc_driver after PGO and LTO
platforms: Linux ELF binaries; rust-lang disabled BOLT for its AArch64 Linux builds because of upstream BOLT bugs
install: cargo install cargo-pgo, plus llvm-bolt and merge-fdata (LLVM 16+ release or the project's Docker image)
one_liner: Profile-driven code layout applied after linking; adds roughly 2-6% on top of PGO in rustc measurements, at a size cost.
how_it_is_fast: BOLT rewrites the linked binary using a profile of which functions and blocks run hot, placing hot code together and moving cold code away. That cuts instruction-cache and page misses in large programs whose hot paths are spread across many functions, which the linker cannot see without a profile.
use_it_when: Large Linux binaries already built with PGO
Programs limited by instruction-cache misses, such as compilers and databases
skip_it_when: Release pipelines that strip symbols: cargo-pgo warns against stripping when using BOLT
caveats: The rust-lang -1.8% is a cycle count, not wall time
tradeoffs: Binary size grew 10.9% (Android) and 48% for librustc_driver.so (rust-lang)
Extra build step with experimental tooling

evidence.quote: Applying BOLT to our toolchain produces a speedup over the baseline compiler of ~24.7% at a size increase of ~10.9%. This is a speedup of ~6.1% over the PGOed compiler without BOLT.
-1.8% mean improvement in cycle counts across many primary benchmarks.
BOLT and Docker support is currently *experimental*.
For the time being, disable bolt on aarch64 due to upstream bolt bugs.
